BURSEVI:v10p313/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p313/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p313/r3.claim: God created everything and proportioned it by giving each thing what enables its perfection and sustenance.
BURSEVI:v10p313/r3.anchor: فسوى خلقه بأن جعل له ما به يتأتى كماله ويتسنى معاشه

BURSEVI:v10p313/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p313/r4.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p313/r4.claim: Al-Qashani reads the verse as God forming the body to receive the perfect spirit, which is ready for every perfection.
BURSEVI:v10p313/r4.anchor: وقال القاشاني : انشأ ظاهرك فعدل بنيتك على وجه قبلت بمزاجه اخاص الروح الأتم

BURSEVI:v10p313/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p313/r5.speaker: النجمي
BURSEVI:v10p313/r5.claim: The Najmiyya reading says each thing is proportioned to receive its prepared share of divine effusion according to its innate capacity.
BURSEVI:v10p313/r5.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية خلق كل شي بحسب الوجود فسوى تسوية بها يصل الفيض الإلهي

BURSEVI:v10p313/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p313/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p313/r6.claim: Another reading says creatures share an equal basic creation but differ because some are specially granted guidance.
BURSEVI:v10p313/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : خلق الخلق فسوى بينهم في الخلقة

QASHANI:87:1-4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:1-4/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:1-4/r2.claim: Creation made the outward human form, then proportioned its constitution with a particular temperament capable of receiving the most complete spirit and all perfections.
QASHANI:87:1-4/r2.anchor: عدل بنيتك على وجه قبلت بمزاجه الخاص الروح الأتم

SULAMI:v2p389#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389#2/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p389#2/r1.claim: God fashioned creation and distinguished people through the special gift of guidance; people should take pride only in guidance and piety, not in their created form (49:13).
SULAMI:v2p389#2/r1.anchor: خلق الخلق فسوى ، وميز بينهم في اختصاص الهداية ، وليس لأحد أن يفتخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r1.claim: The surah selects God's description as Most High because it honors the Quran and steadies its reception; the Quran's dignity follows from being God's speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r1.anchor: وإيثار هذا الوصف في هذه السورة لأنها تضمنت التنويه بالقرآن والتثبيت على تلقيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r4.claim: The object of خلق is omitted and, by the usual rule when context does not specify it, most exegetes including a report from ʿAṭāʾ take it generally as every created thing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r4.anchor: وهو ما قدره جمهور المفسرين ، وروي عن عطاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the omitted object as the human being, while a report from al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes it as Adam, prompted by the pairing with proportioning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يقدر خاصا ، أي خلق الإنسان كما قدره الزجاج ، أو خلق آدم كما روي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r6.claim: The ف in فسوى makes proportioning the main point of the relative clause and presents creation as its groundwork; Ibn Ziyāba's poem supplies a parallel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r6.anchor: وعطف جملة : { فسوى } بالفاء دون الواو للإشارة إلى أن مضمونها هو المقصود من الصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r7.claim: The ف marks sequence in the observer's understanding, since creation is considered before proportioning even though the two occur together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r7.anchor: فالفاء من قوله : { فسوى } للتفريع في الذكر باعتبار أن الخلق مقدم في اعتبار المعتبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r8.claim: If creation is universal, proportioning means making each kind fit its natural activity; a scorpion's curved tail equips it to defend itself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r8.anchor: تسوية ما خلقه فإن حمل على العموم فالتسوية أن جعل كل جنس ونوع من الموجودات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r1.claim: Proportioning accompanies creation and is linked by ف as its resulting effect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r1.anchor: ولكونه مقارنا للخلقة عطف على فعل { خلق } بالفاء المفيدة للتسبب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88/r1.claim: “Then proportioned” means that God fashioned and balanced creation; the explanation was also given at 82:7.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88/r1.anchor: أي فعدل الخلق وقد أشرنا إلى هذا المعنى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r1.claim: God created all creatures and formed every creature in the finest shape.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r1.anchor: خلق الخليقة وسوى كل مخلوق في أحسن الهيئات.

KASHSHAF:87:2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:2/r1.claim: God created everything and formed it with complete integration and proportion, showing it comes from a knowing Creator and wise Maker.
KASHSHAF:87:2/r1.anchor: أي خلق كل شيء فسوّى خلقه تسوية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r4.claim: God created everything and formed it in an ordered, harmonious, well-fitted way, showing that it comes from a knowing and wise maker.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r4.anchor: أي خلق كل شيء فسوى خلقه تسوية

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r7.claim: One interpretation is that God created people and then perfected them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r8.claim: A second interpretation is that God created people complete and made each limb correspond to its proper counterpart.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r9.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r9.claim: He says God created Adam and perfected his form.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r9.anchor: قال الضحاك : خلق آدم فسوى خلقه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r10.claim: A third possible reading is that God created people through His beneficence and made their rulings equal.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r11.claim: A further interpretation places creation in men's loins and proportioning in mothers' wombs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r11.anchor: خلق في أصلاب الرجال , وسوى في أرحام الأمهات

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r12.claim: Another interpretation distinguishes creation of bodies from proportioning of understandings.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#2/r1.claim: God created everything and fashioned it harmoniously, not unevenly or incoherently, with order and evidence of a knowing, wise source; alternatively, He fashioned each thing for its benefit and good.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#2/r1.anchor: أى خلق كل شئ فسوى خلقه تسوية ولم يأت به متفاوتا غير ملتئم

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r1.claim: God fashioned what He created without defect; al-Zajjaj explains the phrase as making the human stature upright.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r1.anchor: أي سوى ما خلق، فلم يكن في خلقه تثبيج. وقال الزجاج: أي عدل قامته.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says God made His creation beautiful.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس حسن ما خلق

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r3.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak specifies that God created Adam and fashioned his form.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: خلق آدم فسوى خلقه.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r4.claim: Other explanations say God created in fathers’ loins and fashioned in mothers’ wombs, created bodies and fashioned understanding, or prepared humans for moral obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r4.anchor: وقيل: خلق في أصلاب الآباء، وسوى في أرحام الأمهات.

NAHHAS:v5p203/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r11.claim: Alladhī is genitive as an adjective of al-aʿlā or rabb; an adjective may itself take an adjective because it shares its referent.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r11.anchor: في موضع جر نعت للأعلى وإن شئت لربك وجاز أن ينعت النعت لأنه المنعوت في المعنى

NAHHAS:v5p203/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r12.claim: The phrase may also be compared with the idiom yā Yazīd al-karīm dhū al-jumma.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r12.anchor: وعلى هذا جاز يا يزيد الكريم ذو الجمة

NAHHAS:v5p203/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r13.claim: He created creatures and fashioned their creation, so that all of it is good in its results.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r13.anchor: ومعنى ( الذي خلق فسوى ) الذي خلق الخلق فعدل خلقه فصار كله حسنا في المفعول

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet loved this surah; Muslim reports that he recited it with al-Ghashiya at Eid and on Friday, sometimes reciting both on one day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] كان يحب هذه السورة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:2/r1.claim: God creates each thing, perfects its making, and brings it to the completeness appropriate to it.

RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r1.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports that the Prophet directed Muslims to say 'glorified is my Lord, the Great' in bowing after 56:74, and 'glorified is my Lord, the Highest' in prostration after 87:1.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r1.anchor: روى عن عقبة بن عامر أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى : { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم }

RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r4.claim: The surrounding context favors exalted power rather than location: spatial distance would not establish worthiness of praise, while creating and proportioning demonstrate power.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r4.anchor: والخالقية تناسب العلو بحسب القدرة لا العلو بحسب الجهة

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.claim: The objection that 'Great' and 'Highest' imply two gods fails because God's oneness is established and the verse never says He is higher than another lord.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية أنه سبحانه وتعالى أعلى من رب آخر

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r6.claim: Creation and guidance answer the implied question of why God merits glorification and form a core proof for God's existence, used by Abraham, Moses, and the first revelations to Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r6.anchor: فكأن سائلا قال : الاشتغال بالتسبيح إنما يكون بعد المعرفة

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r7.claim: The proof from creation and guidance is especially compelling because its wonders are abundant and people can observe them directly.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r7.anchor: العجائب والغرائب في هذه الطريقة أكثر

RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r1.claim: One view restricts creation and proportioning to humans, whose upright stature and beauty resemble the best form praised in another verse.
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r1.anchor: فمن حمله على الإنسان ذكر للتسوية وجوها

RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r2.claim: Another human-specific explanation says humans can perform the actions of all animals through their varied organs and tools.

RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r3.claim: A further human reading takes proportioning to mean preparation for religious obligation and worship.

RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r4.claim: If the verse means all animals, proportioning means giving each the organs, tools, and senses it needs.
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r4.anchor: أعطى كل حيوان ما يحتاج إليه من أعضاء وآلات وحواس

RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r5.claim: If it means all creation, proportioning is God's precise, intentional making of whatever He wills, free of disorder.
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r5.anchor: خلق ما أراد على وفق ما أراد موصوفا بوصف الأحكام والإتقان

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r1.claim: Created can refer specifically to humans, to humans and animals, or to all creation.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r1.anchor: Here created refers to human beings in particular, to human beings and animals, or to all of creation

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r2.claim: On the human-specific reading, God fashioned the first human after breathing His Spirit into him, without irregularity, then measured his form and provided nourishment.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r2.anchor: God fashioned the first human being after breathing into him of His Spirit, leaving him without irregularities

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r3.claim: Qaddara can also be read qadara, meaning to have power or determine, so God retains direct power over all He created.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r3.anchor: Measured out renders qaddara, which can also be read qadara, meaning to have power or to determine

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r4.claim: Guidance may be the instinct by which creatures seek their allotted nourishment, or God’s leading people to religion and knowledge of Unity through signs and proofs.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r4.anchor: Here guidance refers to the instinct God puts in all things to be able to seek the nourishment that He has already measured out for them

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r5.claim: The broader implication is that creation is properly formed without imperfection or flaw.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r5.anchor: The broader implication is that creation is as it should be, without imperfection or flaw

ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r2.claim: God created the human being in balanced form, made him testify that God is his Lord, and created him upon the natural disposition.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r2.anchor: خلق الإنسان مستويا، أشهده على نفسه بأنه ربه.

TABRISI:87:7/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r5.claim: God created creatures and made them alike in sound construction and precision.

TABRISI:87:7/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r6.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:87:7/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī says God created every living being and proportioned its hands, eyes, and legs.
TABRISI:87:7/r6.anchor: خلق كل ذي روح فسوى يديه وعينيه ورجليه عن الكلبي

TABRISI:87:7/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:87:7/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God made the human stature upright rather than inverted like cattle and beasts.
TABRISI:87:7/r7.anchor: خلق الإنسان فعدل قامته عن الزجاج يعني أنه لم يجعله منكوسا كالبهائم والدواب

TABRISI:87:7/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r8.claim: Another account says God made things according to His will and wisdom, shaping them to testify to His oneness.
TABRISI:87:7/r8.anchor: خلق الأشياء على موجب إرادته وحكمته فسوى صنعها لتشهد على وحدانيته

THALABI:v10p183#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p183#2/r7.claim: The following phrase means that God created and proportioned the created form.

ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n1/r1.claim: Creation includes inner coherence and qualities fitted to an entity's intended function, adapting it in advance to its conditions of existence.
ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n1/r1.anchor: He endows it with inner coherence and with qualities consistent with the functions which it is meant to perform

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431/r1.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says God made what He created in the best form; the segment ends mid-comment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431/r1.anchor: قوله: {الذي خلق فسوى} قال عطاء: أحسن ما خلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r1.claim: God created every living being and formed its limbs, including hands, eyes, and legs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r1.anchor: وقال الكلبي: خلق كل ذي روح، فجمع خلقه وسواه: اليدين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r2.claim: God gave every animal the form suited to it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: خلق لكل دابة ما يصلح لها من الخلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r3.claim: God created the human upright; on this interpretation, “formed” means that He straightened the human stature.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحق: خلق الإنسان مستويا (¬5). وعلى هذا معنى: "سوى"

WAHIDI-QT:87:2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:2/r1.claim: God created the human being with a proportionate, well-formed shape.
WAHIDI-QT:87:2/r1.anchor: { الذي خلق فسوى } خلق الانسان مستوي الخلق

ELMALILI:87:2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:2/r1.claim: Because God creates all things, the Creator is above created beings and free from their possibility, origination, and need for a cause; Creator and creature must not be confused in names and attributes.
ELMALILI:87:2/r1.anchor: yaratan Hâlık, yaratılan mahluktan yüksek ve üstündür

ELMALILI:87:2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:2/r2.claim: If al-Aʿlā describes the name, the relative clause would grammatically modify “name,” though creation is properly the act of the named referent; treating the clause independently is preferable.
ELMALILI:87:2/r2.anchor: Bu surette, ٱلَّذِى sıfat olmayıp هُوَ الَّذي takdîrinde cümle-i istînâfiye olmak evlâ olur

ELMALILI:87:2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:2/r3.claim: It is also apt to predicate creation of the name because creation is the effect of the attribute of bringing into being and thus the ruling of the Creator-name; Sunni and Sufi formulations express this relation.
ELMALILI:87:2/r3.anchor: Ehl-i sünnet âlimun bi-ilmihi, kādirun bi-kudretihi, mürîdun bi-irâdetihi

ELMALILI:87:2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:2/r4.claim: God did not leave creation as bare production: He formed it in diverse shapes and regulated it in order, an effect of lordship; Elmalılı calls Him Rabb-i adl.
ELMALILI:87:2/r4.anchor: tesviye etti yarattığını muhtelif suretler içinde düzenine koyup düzgünleştirdi

ELMALILI:87:2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:2/r5.claim: The Lord is superior to those He nurtures.
ELMALILI:87:2/r5.anchor: Şüphe yok ki rab, merbubdan a‘lâ ve üstündür

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.claim: The perfects are aspectual rather than inherently past; verses 4–5 show creation as ongoing world-sustaining activity through the pasture’s recurring growth and decay.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Dass Gottes Schöpfungstätigkeit hier nicht als einmaliger Akt, sondern als fortwährende, welterhaltende Aktivität verstanden wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2:anmerkung/r1.claim: The verbs create and shape also occur together at Q 82:7 and Q 75:38.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r2.claim: Taswiya generally means giving each created kind the structure and form its nature requires; with no stated object here, the verb means giving everything its fitting form (15:29).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r2.anchor: nesnesi belirtilmediğinden– “her şeye uygun şeklini verme” olarak anlamak gerekir

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r1.claim: The relative clause “who created and proportioned” creates a syntactic problem if it modifies Lord, because another adjective intervenes, or if it modifies “name,” since names do not create; the preferred solution makes “Most High” an implied predicate or praise and leaves the object of “created” general.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r1.anchor: ( الذي خلق الخ إن كان صفة للرب كما هو الظاهر لزم الفصل بين الموصوف وصفته بصفة غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r2.claim: Alusi takes “He created all things and proportioned them” broadly: God formed each creation as wisdom requires, with none perfected while another is not; specific readings are too restrictive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r2.anchor: والمراد فجعل خلقه كما تقتضيه حكمته سبحانه في ذاته وصفاته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r3.claim: The verse's universal creation challenges Muʿtazilite claims that humans create their actions; al-Zamakhshari either avoids strict universality or says God enabled human action and bestowed their capacities.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r3.anchor: ورد بما دلت عليه الآية من العموم على المعتزلة في زعمهم أن العبد خالق لأفعاله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi narrows creation and proportioning to every living creature, with its two hands, eyes, and legs made equal; Alusi says the textual ellipsis does not require such a restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r4.anchor: وعن الكلبي خلق كل ذي روح فسوى بين يديه وعينيه ورجليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God created the human and straightened its stature rather than making it inverted like cattle; Alusi likewise regards this as an unsupported narrowing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103#2/r5.anchor: وعن الزجاج خلق الإنسان فعدل قامته ولم يجعله منكوسا كالبهائم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says God created every living being and proportioned its hands, feet, and eyes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: خلق كل ذي روح، فسوى اليدين والرجلين والعينين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r2.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God created humans upright and proportioned their stature.

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r4.claim: God created each thing and fashioned it by giving it what enables its perfection and livelihood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r4.anchor: خلق كل شيء فسوى خلقه بأن جعل له ما به يتأتى كماله ويتم معاشه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395/r1.claim: After mentioning the servants' schemes, the surah commands the Prophet to declare God free of their foul claims; the account of creation and guidance then displays divine power and wisdom and exposes their error.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395/r1.anchor: وكان وقوع ذلك من العبيد المحاط بأعمالهم ودقائق أنفاسهم وأحوالهم من أقبح مرتكب وأبعده عن المعرفة بشيء من عظيم أمر الخالق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r1.claim: God creates and proportionately forms; He assigns each thing its kinds, individuals, measures, qualities, actions and lifespans, fitting striking to the hand, walking to the leg, hearing to the ear and sight to the eye.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r1.anchor: أي أوقع تقديره في أجناس الأشياء وأنواعها وأشخاصها ومقاديرها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها , وغير ذلك من أحوالها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r3.claim: Creation requires proportion to achieve balance, and apportionment requires guidance to achieve completeness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r3.anchor: فالخالق لا بد له من التسوية ليحصل الاعتدال , والتقدير لا بد له من الهداية ليحصل الكمال

DURR-FULL:v8p481/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r1.claim: After the Companions asked what to say in prostration, the sūra was revealed and the Prophet instructed them to say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High.”
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قلنا يا رسول الله كيف نقول في سجودنا فأنزل الله

DURR-FULL:v8p481/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r2.speaker: حضرمى بن عامر
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r2.claim: When Ḥaḍramī recited the verses and added his own line about the pregnant woman, the Prophet told him to add no more, calling the recitation sufficient.
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r2.anchor: عن الكلبي قال: وفد حضرمي بن عامر على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

TAB:87:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:1/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB:87:1/r3.claim: The same wording, Subhana rabbiya al-aʿla alladhi khalaqa fasawwa, is reported as Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s reading.
TAB:87:1/r3.anchor: وهي في قراءة أُبيّ بن كعب كذلك

TAB:87:2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:2/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:2/r1.claim: God created all things and proportioned and adjusted their creation; taswiyah means adjustment.

TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.claim: Verses on divine measure show things descending from undetermined plenitude into particular existence by a determination that precedes and accompanies them, including their relations to other existents.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.anchor: تدل على أن الأشياء تنزل من ساحة الإطلاق إلى مرحلة التعين والتشخص بتقدير منه تعالى

ABUHAYYAN:87:1/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:1/r10.speaker: قالوا
ABUHAYYAN:87:1/r10.claim: Al-aʿlā may qualify rabb or ism; if it qualifies ism, alladhī khalaq cannot then qualify rabb across that intervening modifier.
ABUHAYYAN:87:1/r10.anchor: قالوا : { الأعلى } يصح أن يكون صفة لربك ، وأن يكون صفة لاسم فيكون منصوباً ، وهذا الوجه لا يصح أن يعرب { الذي خلق } صفة لربك

ABUHAYYAN:87:1/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:1/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:1/r11.claim: If alladhī is instead a predicate with an omitted subject or an accusative of praise, al-aʿlā may qualify ism.
ABUHAYYAN:87:1/r11.anchor: فإن لم يجعل الذي صفة لربك ، بل ترفعه على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو تنصبه على المدح ، جاز أن يكون الأعلى صفة لاسم

ABUHAYYAN:87:2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:2/r1.claim: God created everything and formed it proportionately, harmoniously, and perfectly, showing that its maker is knowing and wise.
ABUHAYYAN:87:2/r1.anchor: { الذي خلق } : أي كل شيء ، { فسوى } : أي لم يأت متفاوتاً بل متناسباً على إحكام وإتقان ، دلالة على أنه صادر عن عالم حكيم .

ALUSI:87:1/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r36.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:1/r36.claim: If “who created” modifies Lord, it separates an adjective from its noun with an adjective belonging to another noun; if it modifies “name,” the meaning seems impossible because a name does not create.
ALUSI:87:1/r36.anchor: واستشكل بأن قوله تعالى : { الذى خلق } الخ إن كان صفة للرب كما هو الظاهر لزم الفصل

ALUSI:87:1/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r37.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:1/r37.claim: The reply that “name” means the named, or is inserted so “name of your Lord” equals “your Lord,” is itself questionable.
ALUSI:87:1/r37.anchor: وأجيب باختيار الثاني ولا اختلال إما لأن الاسم بمعنى المسمى أو لأنه لما كان مقحماً كان

ALUSI:87:1/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r38.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:1/r38.claim: The accepted parse makes “who created” the predicate of an omitted subject or an accusative of praise; the object of “created” is omitted, yielding a general meaning.
ALUSI:87:1/r38.anchor: والجواب المقبول إن الذي على ذلك التقدير اما مرفوع على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو منصوب على المدح ومفعول خلق محذوف

ALUSI:87:1/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r39.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:1/r39.claim: Fasawwā originally means making proportionate; God formed every creation in its essence and attributes as His wisdom requires.
ALUSI:87:1/r39.anchor: والمراد فجعل خلقه كما تقتضيه حكمته سبحانه في ذاته وصفاته

ALUSI:87:1/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r40.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:1/r40.claim: One explanation says God made created things alike in their rulings and perfection, not that He perfected some but not others.
ALUSI:87:1/r40.anchor: وفي معناه ما قيل أي فجعل الأشياء سواء في باب الأحكام والإتقان لا أنه سبحانه أتقن بعضاً دون بعض

ALUSI:87:1/r41.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r41.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:1/r41.claim: The verse’s general scope counters the Muʿtazilī claim that human beings create their own acts.
ALUSI:87:1/r41.anchor: ورد بما دلت عليه الآية من العموم على المعتزلة في زعمهم أن العبد خالق لأفعاله

ALUSI:87:1/r42.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r42.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:1/r42.claim: Although al-Zamakhsharī is a Muʿtazilī, he reads the creation broadly; al-Ālūsī suggests he may mean direct or mediated creation, with God enabling human acts and giving people their capacities.
ALUSI:87:1/r42.anchor: والزمخشري مع أن مذهبه مذهبهم قال هنا بالعموم ولعله لم يرد العموم الحقيقي أو أراده لكن على معنى خلق كل شيء

ALUSI:87:1/r43.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r43.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI:87:1/r43.claim: Al-Kalbī narrows the verse to living creatures, proportioning their hands, eyes, and legs.
ALUSI:87:1/r43.anchor: وعن الكلبي خلق كل ذي روح فسوى بين يديه وعينيه ورجليه

ALUSI:87:1/r44.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r44.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI:87:1/r44.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads it as creating the human being and straightening his stature, unlike the inverted form of animals.
ALUSI:87:1/r44.anchor: وعن الزجاج خلق الإنسان فعدل قامته ولم يجعله منكوساً كالبهائم

ALUSI:87:1/r45.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:1/r45.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:1/r45.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds that each restricted reading adds a limitation not supported by the verse’s apparently general wording.
ALUSI:87:1/r45.anchor: وفي كل تخصيص لا يقتضيه ظاهر الحذف

ALUSI:87:2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:2/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:2/r23.claim: If “who created” modifies Lord, it separates an adjective from its noun with an adjective belonging to another noun; if it modifies “name,” the meaning seems impossible because a name does not create.

ALUSI:87:2/r28.speaker: author

ALUSI:87:2/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:2/r30.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI:87:2/r30.claim: Al-Kalbī narrows the verse to living creatures, proportioning their hands, eyes, and legs.
ALUSI:87:2/r30.anchor: وعن الكلبي خلق كل ذي روح فسوى بين يديه وعينيه ورجليه

ALUSI:87:2/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:2/r31.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI:87:2/r31.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads it as creating the human being and straightening his stature, unlike the inverted form of animals.
ALUSI:87:2/r31.anchor: وعن الزجاج خلق الإنسان فعدل قامته ولم يجعله منكوساً كالبهائم

ALUSI:87:2/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:2/r32.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:2/r32.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds that each restricted reading adds a limitation not supported by the verse’s apparently general wording.
ALUSI:87:2/r32.anchor: وفي كل تخصيص لا يقتضيه ظاهر الحذف

BAGHAWI:87:2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI:87:2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says God created every living creature and fashioned its two hands, feet, and eyes.
BAGHAWI:87:2/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي : خلق كل ذي روح ، فسوى اليدين والرجلين والعينين .

BAGHAWI:87:2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI:87:2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God created the human being upright; sawwā means He straightened his stature.
BAGHAWI:87:2/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج : خلق الإنسان مستوياً ، ومعنى سوى : عدل قامته .

BAYDAWI:87:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:2/r1.claim: God created everything and shaped each creation by giving it what enables its perfection and sustains its livelihood.
BAYDAWI:87:2/r1.anchor: خلق كل شيء فسوى خلقه بأن جعل له ما به يتأتى كماله ويتم معاشه

BIQAI:87:2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:2/r1.claim: Creation is bringing things from nonexistence; God can bring about anything He wills, and nothing is difficult for Him.
BIQAI:87:2/r1.anchor: أي أوجد من العدم أي له صفة الإيجاد

BIQAI:87:2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:2/r2.claim: After creating each creature, God proportioned it and supplied what it needs for completion and livelihood, harmonizing the elements despite their opposition; this displays complete knowledge, power, wisdom, and free agency.
BIQAI:87:2/r2.anchor: مع الإيجاد وعقبه التسوية في كل خلق بأن جعل له ما

BIQAI:87:2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:2/r3.claim: Creation develops al-Ṭāriq's question about human origins and demonstrates resurrection; the source links the passage to the day hidden things are exposed.
BIQAI:87:2/r3.anchor: لقوله  "  مم خلق  "  وهو أدل شيء على البعث المذكور

BIQAI:87:2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:2/r4.speaker: الأستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:87:2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the disbelievers' plot in al-Ṭāriq with the command to glorify God, then reads creation, proportion, ordainment, and guidance as evidence of divine power and wisdom against their slander.
BIQAI:87:2/r4.anchor: وقال الاستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

IBNASHUR:87:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:2/r1.claim: The relative clause attributes both creation and the shaping or proportioning of what is created to God.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r1.anchor: وجملة : { الذي خلق فسوى } اشتملت على وصفين : وصف الخلق ووصف تسويه الخلق

IBNASHUR:87:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r2.speaker: الجمهور وعطاء
IBNASHUR:87:2/r2.claim: The majority, with a view also transmitted from Ata, take the omitted object of created as general: God created every creature, as in Moses’ statement at 20:50.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r2.anchor: وهو ما قدره جمهور المفسرين ، وروي عن عطاء ، وهو شأن حذف المفعول إذا لم يدل عليه دليل

IBNASHUR:87:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNASHUR:87:2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes the omitted object to be the human being.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يقدر خاصا ، أي خلق الإنسان كما قدره الزجاج

IBNASHUR:87:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNASHUR:87:2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak takes the omitted object to be Adam, connecting creation with the following shaping clause and 15:29.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r4.anchor: أو خلق آدم كما روي عن الضحاك ، أي بقرينة قرن فعل { خلق } بفعل « سوى »

IBNASHUR:87:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:2/r5.claim: The fa before shaped makes shaping the relative clause’s main point and creation its prelude; Ibn Ziyabah’s poem illustrates a sequence in which grief follows a raid, plunder, and escape.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r5.anchor: وعطف جملة : { فسوى } بالفاء دون الواو للإشارة إلى أن مضمونها هو المقصود من الصلة

IBNASHUR:87:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r6.speaker: ابن زيابة
IBNASHUR:87:2/r6.claim: Ibn Ziyabah’s sequence of dawn attack, taking spoils, and returning witnesses to the ordered actions that justify lament.

IBNASHUR:87:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:2/r7.claim: The fa orders the events in thought and indicates that proportioning follows from creation, although the two occur together.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r7.anchor: فالفاء من قوله : { فسوى } للتفريع في الذكر باعتبار أن الخلق مقدم في اعتبار المعتبر

IBNASHUR:87:2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:2/r8.claim: If creation is general, shaping means making every species suited to its natural activities, as the scorpion’s bent tail equips it for defense.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r8.anchor: والتسوية : تسوية ما خلقه فإن حمل على العموم فالتسوية أن جعل كل جنس ونوع من الموجودات معادلاً

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p340/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p340/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p340/r9.claim: Taswiyah means straightening and making creation precise; restoring the fingertips finely is a metonym for creating them, since nothing is made well-proportioned without being recreated.

IBNATIYYA:87:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:2/r1.claim: Sawwā means He proportioned and perfected creation until its parts became balanced, displaying God's power and oneness.
IBNATIYYA:87:2/r1.anchor: معناه عدل وأتقن حتى صارت الأمور مستوية دالة على قدرته ووحدانيته

IBNKATHIR:87:2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:2/r1.claim: God created all creatures and fashioned each one in the most excellent form.
IBNKATHIR:87:2/r1.anchor: خلق الخليقة وسَوّى كل مخلوق في أحسن الهيئات

MAWARDI:87:2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:2/r1.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:2/r1.claim: One possibility is that God brought people into being and then perfected them.
MAWARDI:87:2/r1.anchor: يعني أنشأ خلقهم ثم سواهم فأكملهم

MAWARDI:87:2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:2/r2.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:2/r2.claim: Another is that He created them fully and made each limb proportionate to its counterpart.
MAWARDI:87:2/r2.anchor: خلقهم خلقا كاملا وسوى لكل جارحة مثلا

MAWARDI:87:2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:2/r3.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:2/r3.claim: A third is that He created them through His favor and equalized them in His rulings; al-Dahhak specifies that He created Adam and fashioned his form.
MAWARDI:87:2/r3.anchor:
خلقهم بإنعامه وسوّى بينهم في أحكامه ،   قال الضحاك :
خلق آدم فَسوّى خلقه

MAWARDI:87:2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:2/r4.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:2/r4.claim: A fourth possibility is that He created in men’s loins and fashioned in mothers’ wombs.
MAWARDI:87:2/r4.anchor: خلق في أصلاب الرجال ،   وسوّى في أرحام الأمهات

MAWARDI:87:2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:2/r5.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:2/r5.claim: A fifth possibility is that He created bodies and fashioned understandings.

NASAFI:87:2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:2/r1.claim: God created everything and fashioned it evenly, not disparate or incoherent but in sound order and proportion, showing that it proceeds from a knowing, wise creator; alternatively, He fashioned each thing for its benefit and good.
NASAFI:87:2/r1.anchor: خلق كل شيء فسوى خلقه تسوية ولم يأت به متفاوتا غير ملتئم

QURTUBI:87:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:2/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi refers to his earlier treatment of taswiya in al-Infitar; here it means forming creation without disorder or flaw.
QURTUBI:87:2/r1.anchor: قد تقدم معنى التسوية في  " الانفطار " وغيرها

QURTUBI:87:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI:87:2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains this as making the human figure upright and proportionate.

QURTUBI:87:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God made beautiful what He created.

QURTUBI:87:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI:87:2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says God created Adam and fashioned his form.
QURTUBI:87:2/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك : خلق آدم فسوى خلقه

QURTUBI:87:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:2/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:2/r5.claim: One explanation distinguishes creation in the fathers' loins from formation in the mothers' wombs.
QURTUBI:87:2/r5.anchor: وقيل : خلق في أصلاب الآباء ، وسوى في أرحام الأمهات

QURTUBI:87:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:2/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:2/r6.claim: Another explanation says God created bodies and then formed their understanding.

QURTUBI:87:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:2/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:2/r7.claim: Another view says God created humanity and prepared it for religious obligation.
QURTUBI:87:2/r7.anchor: وقيل : أي خلق الإنسان وهيأه للتكليف

QURTUBI:87:3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r17.speaker: بعض أشياخي
QURTUBI:87:3/r17.claim: A teacher of al-Qurtubi's said these clauses explain God's exaltedness over all creatures in a way befitting His majesty.
QURTUBI:87:3/r17.anchor: سمعت بعض أشياخي يقول : الذي خلق فسوى وقدر فهدى

RAZI:87:1/r29.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r29.speaker: علي
RAZI:87:1/r29.claim: ʿAlī and Ibn ʿUmar read the command as “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High,” followed by “who created and proportioned”; the wording supplies the commanded glorification.
RAZI:87:1/r29.anchor: قرأ علي عليه السلام وابن عمر : ( سبحان ربي الأعلى

RAZI:87:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r1.claim: After commanding glorification, God answers the implicit question of how the Lord is known by pointing to His creation and guidance.
RAZI:87:2/r1.anchor: لما أمر بالتسبيح ، فكأن سائلا قال :

RAZI:87:2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r2.claim: Rāzī calls creation and guidance a major prophetic proof, citing Abraham’s statement that his Creator guides him.
RAZI:87:2/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم عليه السلام ، أنه قال : { الذي خلقني

RAZI:87:2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r3.claim: Moses answered Pharaoh’s question about the Lord by describing Him as the giver of each thing’s form and its guide.
RAZI:87:2/r3.anchor: قال موسى عليه السلام : { ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

RAZI:87:2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r4.claim: The opening revelation first points to creation and then to teaching, showing the same proof through creation and guidance.
RAZI:87:2/r4.anchor: ثم قال : { اقرأ وربك الأكرم الذي علم بالقلم } وهذا إشارة إلى الهداية

RAZI:87:2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r5.claim: Creation and guidance are especially forceful evidence because their marvels are abundant and humans can observe them closely.
RAZI:87:2/r5.anchor: العجائب والغرائب في هذه الطريقة أكثر

RAZI:87:2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r6.claim: If the phrase concerns humans, proportioning may mean giving them an upright, balanced, beautiful form, as in the description of humanity’s best form.
RAZI:87:2/r6.anchor: جعل قامته مستوية معتدلة وخلقته حسنة

RAZI:87:2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r7.claim: Another human-specific explanation is that people can perform the actions of other animals by means of their varied faculties and tools.
RAZI:87:2/r7.anchor: أما الإنسان فإنه خلق بحيث يمكنه أن يأتي بجميع أفعال الحيوانات بواسطة آلات مختلفة

RAZI:87:2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r8.claim: A third human-specific explanation is that God prepared humanity for religious obligations and worship.
RAZI:87:2/r8.anchor: أنه هيأ للتكليف والقيام بأداء العبادات

RAZI:87:2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r9.claim: If the phrase concerns all animals, proportioning means giving each the limbs, tools, and senses it needs.
RAZI:87:2/r9.anchor: أعطى كل حيوان ما يحتاج إليه من أعضاء وآلات وحواس

RAZI:87:2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r10.claim: If it covers all creation, proportioning means creating each thing as God wills, with perfect order and craftsmanship, since He knows all and can do all possible things.
RAZI:87:2/r10.anchor: خلق ما أراد على وفق ما أراد موصوفا بوصف الأحكام والإتقان

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r4.claim: God creates every living being and arranges its parts and limbs in a wondrous, distinctive structure.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r4.anchor: خلق كل ذي روح فسوى أجزاءه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.claim: The preceding sūrah urges the Prophet to wait: persistent deniers receive only temporary respite under God's practice, and cannot escape His grasp.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.anchor: Sūrah al-Ṭāriq, the previous sūrah ended on urging the Prophet (sws) to show patience and to wait for the decision of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.claim: This sūrah shifts its primary address from stubborn Quraysh to the Prophet and, over at least ten following sūrahs, dispels his preaching fears in varied ways.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.anchor: while ignoring these stubborn elements from among the Quraysh, the Prophet (sws) is addressed directly and given glad tidings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.claim: Verses 1–5 direct the Prophet to glorify God, whose attributes show that creation and human physical and intellectual capacities mature gradually.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r5.claim: God's works and plans unfold gradually according to wisdom; people should patiently fulfill His directives, since delays are wise and hardships benefit them in both lives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r5.anchor: all of Almighty’s works and plans are carried out in a gradual manner – a scheme which itself is totally based on His wisdom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r6.claim: Khalaqa can mean making a sketch or effigy as well as creating; the cited bird example illustrates that sense, while contextual taswiyah means perfecting.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r6.anchor: it also means “to make a sketch or an effigy of something.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r1.claim: Human creation is not instantaneous: an initial sketch passes through stages until the person reaches completion; taswiyah can mean improving, flattening, or perfecting, and context selects perfection.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r4.claim: The word taswiyah can denote improving, flattening, or perfecting; the context chooses the sense of perfecting.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r4.anchor: here it is used in the last of these meanings

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r7.claim: God created everything and proportioned it without disparity, with fitting harmony and precision that indicate a knowing, wise creator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r7.anchor: الذي خلق: أي كل شيء، فسوى: أي لم يأت متفاوتا بل متناسبا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r11.claim: God creates from nothing and can bring about whatever He wills without difficulty.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r11.anchor: أي أوجد من العدم أي له صفة الإيجاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r12.claim: Creation is followed by proportioning each creature for its perfection and livelihood, balancing conflicting elements through complete knowledge and power.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r12.anchor: أوقع مع الإيجاد وعقبه التسوية في كل خلق بأن جعل له ما يتأتى معه كماله ويتم معاشه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r13.claim: The balancing of opposed temperaments demonstrates God's wisdom and freely chosen action.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r13.anchor: وذلك بالعلم التام والقدرة الكاملة دلالة على تمام حكمته وفعله بالاختيار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.claim: Its purposes include glorifying God and indicating His oneness through His unique creation of humans and earthly sustenance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.anchor: تنزيه الله تعالى والإشارة إلى وحدانيته لانفراده بخلق الإنسان وخلق ما في الأرض مما فيه بقاؤه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.claim: Proportioning and guidance suit the surah because God who fashioned the Prophet for the burdens of mission also equips him to retain revelation and grants him an easy law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.anchor: الذي يسوي خلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تسوية تلائم ما خلقه لأجله من تحمل أعباء الرسالة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r3.claim: Sawwa means proportioned and perfected creation so its order displays God's power and oneness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r3.anchor: معناه عدل وأتقن حتى صارت الأمور مستوية دالة على قدرته ووحدانيته

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.claim: The surah follows the preceding warning of unbelievers with God’s attributes and power to do whatever He wills.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.anchor:
ما يشاء.
(بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم)
قوله تعالى:

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r6.claim: Taswiyah is making things equal in a respect, whether in form, rank, status, or another feature.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r6.anchor: التسوية: الجمع بين شيئين بما هما فيه سواء، سوى يسوي تسوية، ثم قد يكون في الصورة

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r17.claim: Fasawwā may mean He made the creature’s form, limbs, and senses proportionate, or fashioned it as He intended without deficiency or ugliness, according to Abu Ali.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r17.anchor: فسوى قيل: سوى: عدل، أي: سوى خلقه وأعضاءه وحواسه، وقيل: سوى صنعها على ما أراد

MUQATIL:87:1-7/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r2.claim: God creates a person in the womb through the stages of a drop, a clot, and a morsel of flesh, then proportionately forms him.
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r2.anchor: الإنسان في بطن أمه من نطفة، ثم من علقة، ثم من مضغة،

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r9.claim: Creating gathers parts; fashioning makes them proportionate and places each where it belongs.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r9.anchor: خلق الشيء جمع أجزائه، وتسويته جعلها متساوية بحيث يوضع كل في موضعه

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r10.claim: Creation and fashioning here cover composed creatures; the first four verses describe divine governance and prove absolute lordship.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r10.anchor: والخلق والتسوية وإن كانا مطلقين لكنهما إنما يشملان ما فيه تركيب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r2.claim: God created the human being well-proportioned.

TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.claim: Guidance is of two kinds: creational direction of each kind and individual toward its created perfection, acts, appointed course, and lifespan; the Qur'an describes God as giving each thing its form and then guiding it.
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.anchor: وهدايته تعالى نوعان أحدهما الهداية التكوينية وهي التي تتعلق بالأمور التكوينية
